http://www.heraldglobe.com/news/27924218.text: NATO scrambles warplanes to shoot down drone over Latvia RT.com 14 Aug 2026, 20:26 GMT+10 Ukraine was carrying out a major UAV raid against Russias Leningrad region at the time A NATO fighter jet has destroyed a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the US-led bloc has said. The announcement came as Ukraine carried out a major UAV attack against Russia's northwestern Leningrad Region on Friday. A total of 54 drones were shot down or intercepted above the region overnight, local governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said. A fire broke out at the key Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga during the raid, but it was swiftly extinguished, according to the governor. There have been multiple reports in recent months of Ukrainian drones violating the airspace of Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, and Finland, or crashing inside those countries, while on their way to Russia. NATO spokesperson Allison Hart said on Friday that "this morning, we saw Italian Eurofighters based in Lithuania and Turkish F-16s out of Estonia scramble, with one Eurofighter downing a drone over Latvian airspace." The Latvian Defense Ministry also confirmed the incident, saying in a statement that "fighter jets participating in the NATO Baltic Air Policing mission successfully shot down a foreign unmanned aerial vehicle." The ministry claimed that the UAV "entered Latvia as a result of Russian electronic warfare activities." "Similar incidents involving foreign unmanned aerial vehicles entering or approaching Latvian airspace may occur" as long as the conflict between Russia and Ukraine continues, the statement added. Last week, Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania issued a joint demarche after Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin said Moscow had "verified data," showing that Baltic states had provided air corridors for Ukrainian drones attacking Russian civilian infrastructure. The governments in Riga, Tallinn, and Vilnius denied Galuzin's accusations as "completely unfounded." On Thursday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the Russian military and intelligence services "see where things fly from and how they fly," referring to incoming UAVs. "This is well-known to everyone, and we are not going to prove anything to anyone here," Peskov stressed. READ MORE: Moscow rebuffs Baltic protest over Ukrainian drones Moscow previously warned that if Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania knowingly help to facilitate Ukrainian drone strikes, Russia could consider them complicit in the attacks and would have the right to self-defense under the UN Charter. Europe Poland Begins Construction of Razor-Wire Barrier Along Border With Russia’s Kaliningrad Amid Security Concerns Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Poland's Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki and defense minister Mariusz Blaszczak meet with service members near the frontier, as hundreds of migrants gather on the Belarusian side of the border with Poland in an attempt to cross it, near Kuznica in Bialostocka, Poland, on Nov. 9, 2021. Polish Prime Minister's Office/Handout via Reuters Katabella Roberts 11/2/2022 | Updated: 11/3/2022 0:00 X 1 Poland has begun constructing a razor-wire fence on its border with Russia’s Kaliningrad, where Moscow has a significant military presence, officials said on Nov. 2. Polish Defense Minister Mariusz Blaszczak told reporters at a news conference that he has ordered the temporary barrier to be built immediately to ensure that Poland is secure. The barrier will measure 2.5 meters (eight feet) high and three meters (10 feet) deep along the 210-kilometer (130-mile) border. Błaszczak cited security concerns as the reason behind the construction at the border, which comes amid ongoing tensions with Russia over its invasion of Ukraine. Warsaw is also concerned that the Kremlin plans to facilitate illegal border crossings by Asian and African immigrants in an effort to destabilize Europe, concerns prompted by a recent decision by Russia’s aviation authority to launch flights from the Middle East and North Africa to Kaliningrad. The border area, which is patrolled by border guards, has no physical barrier. Polish soldiers specializing in demining began carrying out the initial prep work on Nov. 2. The barrier is due to be completed by the end of 2023, Błaszczak said. He referenced the 2021 crisis during which thousands of African and Middle Eastern illegal aliens attempted to cross the border of Belarus, a close ally of Russia, into Poland. Many of those border crossers died, and Poland subsequently erected a steel wall on the Belarus border to stem the flow of illegal immigrants. That border was completed in June. At the time, Polish and other European Union leaders accused Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko’s government of encouraging immigrants from the Middle East to travel to Minsk and make their way into Europe. Belarus officials denied those claims. A member of the Ukrainian State Border Guard Service stands near the border with Belarus and Poland in the Volyn region of Ukraine on Nov. 16, 2021. Gleb Garanich/Reuters Poland–Russia Border ‘Stable and Calm’ Human rights groups then accused Poland of double standards after the nation welcomed an influx of Ukrainians fleeing Russia’s invasion while simultaneously moving to prevent Middle Eastern and North African migrants from entering via the Belarus border. “If you give a lift to a refugee at the Ukrainian border, you are a hero. If you do it at the Belarus border, you are a smuggler and could end up in jail for eight years,” said Natalia Gebert, founder and CEO of Dom Otwarty, or Open House, a Polish nongovernmental organization that helps refugees, according to a June report by The Associated Press . Kaliningrad is a semi-exclave—a portion of a country that’s geographically separated from the main part by a surrounding foreign territory—that lies on the Baltic Sea and is sandwiched between Poland and Lithuania and separated from Belarus by a border corridor. Despite there being no barrier along the border, a spokesperson for the Polish Border Guard told Reuters that there were no illegal entries from Kaliningrad into Poland in October. “The Polish–Russian border is stable and calm. There has been no illegal crossing of the border,“ Polish border spokesperson Anna Michalska said. ”We are not only there in times of peace. We are prepared for various crisis situations, and after what happened on the Polish–Belarusian border, we are even more prepared for everything, for all of the darkest scenarios.” The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report. https://www.dw.com/en/how-prepared-is-ke.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OHK4 Kenya is on high alert after the country reported one death from Ebola and a second case Image: Monicah Mwangi/REUTERS Advertisement Kenya is rushing to contain Ebola cases linked to the deadliest outbreak on record in the Democratic Republic of Congo . The East African nation has reported two cases and one death. The DRC has reported more than 9,000 cases and 4,400 deaths. Kenya's first Ebola patient died at Nairobi hospital on October 5. The 40-year-old Kenyan had traveled by road from the DRC to Uganda before boarding a flight to Nairobi in Entebbe on October 3. One of his relatives is now confirmed to have contracted the virus. The 39-year-old was under quarantine when he developed symptoms on October 13. "Both cases are linked, and ​there is no evidence of spread in the wider community," Kenya's health ministry said. Contact tracing has been ongoing since officials first detected the case. Of the 128 people who came into contact with the first Ebola patient, 113 have been identified, according to the health ministry. All, except five — who are in unspecified countries abroad—have been quarantined. Should Kenyans worry about Ebola spreading? Public anxiety is rising, along with fears of lockdowns and economic disruption, and skepticism about government readiness. "It's a very dangerous disease, so it's very shocking," a Nairobi resident told DW. Another citizen said he was disappointed: "The government has been caught unaware. It appears to me that the government was not prepared, especially at the entry point of this particular person who was found to be suffering from Ebola." One woman said she felt there was a lack of public information on the disease. "The government should do more in educating and sensitizing about it, and raising awareness," she said. Kenya's Health Ministry, through Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, has been seeking to allay fears, urging Kenyans to remain vigilant and encouraging anyone who develops symptoms to report to the nearest medical facility. According to the World Health Organization (WHO) , symptoms can develop between two and 21 days after infection. Early symptoms include: fever, fatigue, malaise, muscle pain, headache and sore throat. Later, a patient may suffer from vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and kidney and liver infection. However, these symptoms might be similar to other illnesses such as malaria or typhoid, and only an Ebola test can confirm if one has been exposed to the virus. Kenya's Minster of Health Aden Duale (left) has sought to calm the nation as health officials rush to contain the virus from spreading Image: Monicah Mwangi/REUTERS Criticism and calls to improve screening Several prominent figures, medical unions and opposition politicians have criticized Kenya's response to its first Ebola cases. Former Chief Justice David Maraga, who has declared interest in running for the presidency in the 2027 election, questioned how a man carrying the Ebola virus could pass through screening at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, Nairobi. "We don't know how many have been infected. We must demand appropriate action be taken so that we don't have deaths arising from that disease," Maraga told The Standard . Kalonzo Musyoka, Kenya's vice president from 2008 to 2013, meanwhile noted that doctors at Nairobi Hospital, not border systems, detected the danger. A hand santitation station at the Kenya-Uganda border Image: James Keyi/REUTERS Dennis Miskellah of the Kenya Medical Practitioners, Pharmacists and Dentists Union believes that the Ebola cases show that Kenya's health system is not pandemic-ready. "This system is not yet resilient. This system did not learn from the COVID pandemic that we had a few years ago," he said. "Since May, we've had this outbreak in the region. Uganda, our immediate neighbor, had almost 20 cases. So, we had ample time to prepare adequately. But it seems like somebody dropped the ball." Kenya went on high alert after the DRC declared the Ebola outbreak in May. The government designated several hospitals as isolation centers. It also enhanced screening at airports and border points, deploying mobile labs. Flights from several African countries were ordered to land in designated airport wings for screening. Where are the gaps in Kenya's health system? "Top of it all is that there's has been a serious lapse of leadership in governance of healthcare this country," said Miskellah. "All those broken pillars, there's no clear responsibility or chain of command, whether its the Ministry of Health or the 47 county governments who are semi-automous." Capacity at some isolation centers is limited. Rural facilities lack resources such as the protective gear available at major hospitals, according to Miskellah. And there's also a shortage of health workers due to a freeze on public service workers. Meanwhile, healthcare workers, many of whom have no healthcare cover, are reportedly wary of putting their lives at risk. Dozens of Kenyan nurses and doctors lost their lives during the COVID-19 pandemic. What makes this Ebola outbreak different To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Kenya's agreements on Ebola with its neighbors are being called into question since the first case was recorded in Kenya, which has one of the strongest healthcare systems in the region. Experts are questioning the state of regional cooperation on Ebola, given that borders have largely remained open despite the surge in cases and deaths. "Before we trust these agreements and cooperation, then we have have to audit them and question them so that we don't just blindly believe that Kenya is doing the right thing, or that the DRC is doing the right thing," said Miskellah. Then, there's the question of individual responsibility. Kenya requires travelers arriving from Congo, Uganda, Tanzania , Ethiopia , Angola , Zambia , Rwanda , Burundi , Central African Republic and South Sudan to complete a health declaration form — truthfully. Photograph: Ross D Franklin/AP Arizona University of Arizona sorority member alleges sexual assault at fraternity house Student told the university’s police department that assault by two men occurred in August during a night of drinking Associated Press Tue 20 Oct 2026 22.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A sorority member at the University of Arizona has alleged she was sexually assaulted by two men at a fraternity house during a night of drinking in late August. The student told the university’s police department that she consensually kissed one of the men at one point while at the Sigma Phi Epsilon house on 26 August but doesn’t remember agreeing to sex, according to search warrant records posted Monday night by KOLD-TV in Tucson. The sexual assault allegations surfaced two weeks after the university had suspended activities for its 21 fraternities amid reports of misconduct, including assault, hazing and drug- and alcohol-related behavior. Suspensions on all but five fraternities have since been lifted after they had mandatory meetings with the dean of students. In speaking with an investigator, the sorority member recalled consuming tequila, including sharing a cup of the beverage with friends; witnessing two men sexually assaulting her, and even feeling one man’s breath on her face; awakening the next morning without pants or underwear on; and noticing a difficulty in swallowing, a possible sign of strangulation, according to the records. Later that day, she reported the allegations to police and underwent a forensic exam at a hospital. In a recorded call with the sorority member two days after the encounter, one of the men acknowledged he had sex with her, but said she had agreed to it and denied that another man had had sex with her. He said he had been drunk and “fuzzy” on what happened. He said people took video of the sorority member and him kissing in a bathroom, according to the records. The Associated Press left email and phone messages with the university Tuesday seeking comment. Its police department said the investigation is ongoing and declined to say whether any arrests had been made. The Pima county attorney’s office said the case hadn’t been referred to it for prosecution. The university put Sigma Phi Epsilon on probation from July until May of next year after a hazing complaint. Sigma Phi Epsilon isn’t among the five fraternities that are currently listed as suspended. The national fraternity organization said they ordered members of the Arizona chapter to comply with any investigation. “The Fraternity has suspended those involved while the investigation proceeds. Any member found responsible will be expelled from Sigma Phi Epsilon, and we will cooperate fully with law enforcement as it seeks accountability under the law,” read a statement from Brian Warren, chief executive officer of Sigma Phi Epsilon. Retaliation against the alleged victim or any witnesses would also not be tolerated, Warren said. Other cases of alleged sexual assault at fraternities have drawn recent national attention. At Cornell University, a former student alleged that multiple Chi Phi fraternity members sexually assaulted her in October 2024. The allegations have sparked campus protests, renewed scrutiny of the Ivy League school’s disciplinary system and a state investigation into the alleged assault. Several of the men have denied that they engaged in any nonconsensual sex or denied they touched the woman at all. This week, a woman sued Alpha Delta Phi and its Chicago chapter, alleging she was raped in February by a member of the fraternity at the University of Chicago. The woman, identified in the lawsuit as Jane Doe, claimed she was sexually assaulted during a party at an on-campus residence and that she reported the assault to city police the next day. When asked about the case, Chicago police did not name the fraternity or provide an exact address, but said they were investigating a report of a sexual assault that happened on the same block early on 8 February. The University of Chicago and Alpha Delta Phi did not respond to emails in time for publication. Chicago police are also investigating after a woman reported being sexually assaulted during a party at another fraternity earlier this month. The University of Chicago said in a statement last week that a woman reported being sexually assaulted at the Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity house. The fraternity said none of its members took part in the alleged attack.
